From ae05340ccaa9d347fe85415609e075545bec589f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yochai Eisenrich <echelonh@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 00:49:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: ipv6: ndisc: fix ndisc_ra_useropt to initialize
 nduseropt_padX fields to zero to prevent an info-leak

When processing Router Advertisements with user options the kernel
builds an RTM_NEWNDUSEROPT netlink message. The nduseroptmsg struct
has three padding fields that are never zeroed and can leak kernel data

The fix is simple, just zeroes the padding fields.

Fixes: 31910575a9de ("[IPv6]: Export userland ND options through netlink (RDNSS support)")
Signed-off-by: Yochai Eisenrich <echelonh@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260324224925.2437775-1-echelonh@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ndisc.c b/net/ipv6/ndisc.c
index f6a5d8c73af9..186e60c79214 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/ndisc.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/ndisc.c
@@ -1209,6 +1209,9 @@ static void ndisc_ra_useropt(struct sk_buff *ra, struct nd_opt_hdr *opt)
 	ndmsg->nduseropt_icmp_type = icmp6h->icmp6_type;
 	ndmsg->nduseropt_icmp_code = icmp6h->icmp6_code;
 	ndmsg->nduseropt_opts_len = opt->nd_opt_len << 3;
+	ndmsg->nduseropt_pad1 = 0;
+	ndmsg->nduseropt_pad2 = 0;
+	ndmsg->nduseropt_pad3 = 0;
 
 	memcpy(ndmsg + 1, opt, opt->nd_opt_len << 3);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/ipv6/ndisc.c`

The patch adds three lines to the `ndisc_ra_useropt()` function, initializing the padding fields of the `nduseroptmsg` structure to zero:

```c
ndmsg->nduseropt_pad1 = 0;
ndmsg->nduseropt_pad2 = 0;
ndmsg->nduseropt_pad3 = 0;
```

These are inserted into the function just after the other `ndmsg` fields are assigned and before user option data is copied into the message.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The three modifications are directly related – they all serve the same purpose: preventing an information leak. Prior to the patch, the `nduseroptmsg` structure's padding fields (`nduseropt_pad1`, `nduseropt_pad2`, `nduseropt_pad3`) were left uninitialized, potentially exposing kernel stack memory to user space via the `RTM_NEWNDUSEROPT` netlink message. By explicitly zeroing these fields, the patch ensures no sensitive data leaks through the padding. The fix is minimal, targeted, and addresses the root cause of the security vulnerability.
